rules.title: The scroll goes through one module
rules.how: No script reads window.scrollY / scrollX / pageYOffset or the root's scrollTop, listens to the window's (or document's) scroll, or scrolls the window, outside the scroll module (src/scripts/scroller.js). In Safari on a Mac the page may scroll in its own box (runtime/scroller.js): the window's scroll then never changes. Ask the module: y(), to(), onScroll(). (read from the code).

rules.title: Observers that look ahead watch from the scroller
rules.how: Every IntersectionObserver with a rootMargin also names its root (the scroll module's ioRoot): in the box the box clips what is in it, so seen from the screen nothing below it would ever be "near" and nothing loads. (read from the code).

rules.title: WebGL only on a real GPU
rules.how: Every getContext("webgl"/"webgl2") (and three.js WebGLRenderer) asks for failIfMajorPerformanceCaveat or reads the renderer's name right after (software: SwiftShader, llvmpipe), or goes through runtime/gpu.js. Without a GPU, Chrome copies a WebGL canvas back to the processor every frame (≈ 12 ms a frame for one ring of covers). (read from the code).

rules.title: Nothing waits for a load that has passed
rules.how: No addEventListener("load") on the window unless the line or the three above check document.readyState: a script that starts late (after the first frame, imported on demand) comes after the load, and the listener never runs. Use whenLoaded(fn) (runtime/loaded.js). (read from the code).

rules.title: The start-up waits for the stylesheets
rules.how: The entry script waits for every stylesheet (runtime/styles.js stylesReady(), or the same wait written out) before its first call of anything it imports: Safari may run a module before the stylesheet applies (WebKit bug 261655), and what is measured then stays wrong. (read from the code).

rules.title: Third parties start only after consent
rules.how: — (read from the code).
rules.note: turned off by the adapter (rules.learnings.consent: false)

rules.title: A stylesheet loaded on its own imports the custom media
rules.how: Every stylesheet the pages or the scripts load (an entry) has, in its @import closure, the file of the custom media (src/styles/base/media.css) when any file of that closure uses one: Lightning CSS (Vite) defines a custom media per bundle, and fails on (or drops) one it has not seen. (read from the code).

rules.title: The bottom bar's guard stays empty
rules.how: No rule for .bar-guard gives it a background, a backdrop filter, content or pointer-events: none: Safari skips it as see-through only while it has nothing to show and takes taps (a backdrop filter made the bar white; runtime/safari.css). (read from the code).

rules.title: Every page with the box runs the box script first
rules.how: Every page that has the page's box ([data-page]) runs the box script (node_modules/site-kit/runtime/box.js) in its <head>, before any other script: else Safari on a Mac scrolls that page in the window (a glass bar), and scripts that ask the scroll module read the wrong scroller. (read from the code).
